messages.subject: N specification in running sumstats
parts:
A somewhat basic question, but here it goes.  If GWAS include SNP specific N, and I munged using SNP specific N, then running sumstats should I specify N=NULL or N=c(NA,NA,NA)?  

Thanks for any help!
Dan

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: N specification in running sumstats
parts:
Hi Dan, 

Good question! Either should work. If you write N = NULL then the package will make a vector of NAs based on the number of files you feed it, so the end result is the same as providing a vector of NAs. Bottom line: N = NULL is probably the most straightforward. 

The different specifications have to do with how the partially standardized beta (a GWAS beta standardized with respect to the variance in the phenotype but not the predictor [the genotype] is backed out from the data. If you are working with, for example, Z-stats only for a binary outcome vs. logistic betas vs. OLS betas then the way that partially standardized beta is backed out is going to differ. The logic for this is described in the method section of the original 2019 Genomic SEM paper. 

Best, 
  Andrew
